title: Flat rate vs reducing rate
blurb: Two loans can both say 10% and still cost very different amounts. Learn to compare by total repaid.
t1.title: Why "10% flat" is a trick of the eye
t1.b1: Ravi sees an ad: "Loan at only {exF} flat!" It sounds like {exF} a year. He wants to know if it really is.
t1.b2: With a **flat rate**, interest is worked out on the full amount for the whole time. Repaying part of it changes nothing.
t1.b3: Imagine a ledger that keeps charging you on the full amount, though each month you owe a little less. That is how a flat rate works.
t1.b4.1: Example: borrow {exP} at {exF} flat for {exY} years.
t1.b4.2: Interest = {exP} x {exF} x {exY} years, added to the loan.
q1.prompt: Meena borrows {P} at {F} flat for {Y} years. What is her monthly payment? Type a number in rupees.
q1.hint: Add the flat interest ({P} x {F} x {Y}) to the loan, then divide by {months} months.
q2.prompt: How much does Meena repay in total over {months} months? Type a number in rupees.
t2.title: Reducing balance: the fairer count
t2.b1: With a **reducing balance** loan, interest is charged only on what you still owe. As you repay, the interest part shrinks.
t2.b2: Most EMI loans of the kind you saw before use a reducing balance. A flat rate charges on the full amount all along, so the same number costs far more.
q3.prompt: Which loan charges interest only on the amount you still owe?
q3.explain: A reducing balance loan charges interest on the shrinking amount you still owe.
q4.prompt: Two loans both say "{exF}". One is flat, one is reducing. Which costs more in total?
q4.hint: Flat charges on the full amount for the whole time.
q4.explain: The flat loan costs more, because it keeps charging on money you have already repaid.
t3.title: Lab: the real yearly rate
t3.b1.prompt: Open the lab. Change the flat rate and the years. Compare the flat rate you were told with the real yearly rate.
t3.b2: Many people read "{exF} flat" as "{exF} a year". The real yearly rate is much higher, about {exReal} in our example, because you owe less as you repay.
q5.prompt: In the lab, use {P}, a flat rate of {F} and {Y} years. What is the real yearly rate? Type a percentage.
q5.hint: Read the red "Real yearly rate" in the lab.
q5.explain: A flat rate of {F} is really about {real1} a year.
q6.prompt: A lender advertises "{F} flat". What is true about the real yearly rate?
q6.hint: Check the lab: compare the flat rate with the real rate.
q6.explain: The real yearly rate is always higher than the flat rate. Here it is {real1}.
q6.opt.a: It is {F} a year, the same number.
q6.fb.a: A flat rate is not a yearly rate. You owe less each month but the flat rate keeps charging on the full amount, so the real rate is higher.
q6.opt.b: It is higher than {F} a year.
q6.opt.c: It is lower than {F} a year.
t4.title: Compare by total repaid
t4.b1: Headline rates hide how the interest is counted. To compare two offers fairly, find the **total repaid** on each one. The offer with the smaller total costs less.
t4.b2.1: Offer A: {oP} at {oFlat} flat for {oY} years.
t4.b2.2: Offer B: {oP} at {oRed} on a reducing balance for {oM} months.
t4.b2.3: Work out the total repaid on each, then compare.
q7.prompt: Offer A repays {oFlatTotal} in total. Offer B is a reducing loan and repays {oRedTotal}. How many rupees cheaper is B? Type a number.
q7.hint: Subtract the smaller total from the bigger one.
q7.explain: {oFlatTotal} minus {oRedTotal} is {oGap}. B is cheaper by that much.
q8.prompt: Offer A says {oFlat} flat. Offer B says {oRed} reducing. Which one costs less overall?
q8.hint: Compare the totals repaid, not the headline numbers.
q8.explain: B costs less in total, even though its headline rate looks higher.
q8.opt.a: Offer A, because {oFlat} is lower than {oRed}
q8.fb.a: A lower headline rate is not always cheaper. A flat rate and a reducing rate are counted differently, so compare the totals.
q8.opt.b: Offer B, because it repays less in total
q8.opt.c: You cannot tell from these numbers
t5.title: Read the numbers before signing
t5.b1: Before you sign, ask for these in writing. Check the total you repay, the type of rate, the months and any fees. If something is unclear, do not sign yet.
q9.prompt: Which paper detail helps you compare two loan offers best?
q9.hint: It is the number that includes everything you pay.
q9.explain: The total repaid, in writing, is the fairest way to compare.
q9.opt.a: The biggest number in the advert
q9.opt.b: The size of the monthly payment only
q10.prompt: Challenge: Offer A at {oFlat} flat for {oY} years on {oP}. What is its real yearly rate? Use the lab. Type a percentage.
q10.hint: Set the lab to {oP}, {oFlat} flat and {oY} years. Read the real rate.
q10.explain: Offer A is really charging about {oReal} a year.
glossary.borrow_flat_rate.def: Interest worked out on the full amount borrowed, for the whole loan.
glossary.borrow_reducing.def: Interest charged only on the part of the loan you still owe.
glossary.borrow_real_rate.def: The true yearly rate a loan charges once the repayments are counted.
